title: Default editor chat to Agent Host Copilot when the agent host is enabled
body:
Makes **Agent Host Copilot** the default editor chat provider when the agent host is enabled, so first-time users start on Copilot instead of the Local harness. Local remains fully visible and selectable, and any explicit or remembered choice still wins.

The default is now driven by `chat.agentHost.enabled` (read only via `IAgentHostEnablementService`). The experimental `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` setting is kept, but only for the one-time Local→Copilot migration.

## Default provider for a new editor chat (no remembered/current selection)

| `chat.agentHost.enabled` | `chat.editor.localAgent.enabled` | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| true | (any) | Agent Host Copilot |
| false | true | Local |
| false | false | First visible non-local provider, else Local |

Any **explicit override** or **remembered** (previously picked) selection takes precedence over the table above. A remembered **Local** selection is honored as a real opt-out: empty Local sessions are no longer auto-replaced/skipped in its favor (both the editor and the sidebar).

## `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` (one-time migration)

Only has an effect when the agent host is enabled. It migrates an existing user off Local exactly once:

| Interaction | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| First "New Chat" from a Local session (setting on, not yet applied) | Switch to Agent Host Copilot once, then persist a per-profile "applied" flag |
| Every interaction after that | No further auto-switch — remembered/current selection wins (returning to Local stays Local) |
| Agent host disabled (e.g. web) | Swap never fires — no unresolvable Agent Host URI and the flag is not written |

## Other behavior changes

- **`preferCopilotHarness` is now scoped only to the one-time migration.** It no longer controls the default provider (that is now `chat.agentHost.enabled`) and no longer affects picker visibility.
- **Local's visibility is governed solely by `chat.editor.localAgent.enabled`.** Local is hidden when that setting is `false` and a non-local provider is available; it stays visible in virtual workspaces or when it would otherwise be the only option. Previously, `preferCopilotHarness` + a disabled local agent could hide Local unconditionally, even as the last-resort option.

title: sessions: move read/unread ownership to sessions providers
body:
## What

Moves ownership of session **read/unread** state in the Agents window from the UI layer (`SessionsListModelService`) to the **sessions providers**, surfaced through the provider-owned `ISession.isRead` observable. Existing locally-stored read state is migrated once so previously-read sessions don't suddenly appear unread after upgrade.

## Why

Read/unread previously lived entirely in the client view (a `readSessions` set + a cutoff date) and was never persisted by providers. That made the state UI-specific and inconsistent across surfaces. Making it provider-owned gives a single source of truth (`ISession.isRead`) shared by the session list, the session header, and the picker.

## Changes

- **Provider-owned read state.** `ISessionsProvider.setSessionReadState(sessionId, isRead)` is the write path; `ISession.isRead` is the read path. The management service exposes `markRead`/`markUnread`/`setSessionReadState`.
- **Unread on turn completion**, implemented per provider so a background session that produces new output while unwatched shows as unread:
  - **AgentHost** (local + remote, shared `agentSideEffects.ts`): server marks the session unread when a turn completes, is **cancelled**, or **errors** — including background subagent turns.
  - **Local chat**: provider marks unread on any `inProgress → terminal` transition.
  - **Copilot chat**: provider marks unread on any `InProgress → terminal (not Untitled)` transition, routed through the backing agent session model.
- **`ISession.isRead` is the single source of truth.** The active session is persisted as read from the sessions service (viewing a session — mouse, keyboard, or programmatic — marks it read), so the list, header, and picker all read the provider flag directly with no display-only overlay.
- **Additive one-time migration** of legacy read state: only ever marks sessions *read* (never unread), guarded by a one-shot done-flag plus an `updatedAt` cutoff, so a later legitimate unread is never flipped back.
- **Cache-key bump to `.v2`** for the agent-host session caches to discard stale persisted `isRead: true` artifacts that would otherwise mask the server bit on upgrade.

## Notes for reviewers

- The migration is intentionally **read-only/additive** — see `migrateLegacyReadState` in `sessionsListModelService.ts` (kept behind a `TODO@sandy081` cleanup marker).
- New tests cover: turn complete / cancelled / errored / subagent unread (agent host), local + copilot transition unread, additive migration, legacy-cache discard, and the active-session-persisted-read behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Codex agent: MCP tools + customizations parity (config pickup, auth, .agents, client plugins)
body:
## Overview

Brings the **codex** agent in the agent host protocol (AHP) to parity with the copilot/claude agents for MCP tools and customizations. Previously the codex agent had read-back MCP scaffolding but was never told which servers to run, couldn't pick up config changes, couldn't authenticate OAuth-gated MCP servers, and didn't surface the full set of customizations. Each concern is a focused commit.

All changes are scoped to `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/` (+ its tests). Verified end-to-end in the Agents window against the real codex binary (v0.142.0).

## What changed

### MCP servers are now launched, per session
- **Launch workbench-configured MCP servers** — the root `mcpServers` config (the same set copilot forwards to its SDK) is now passed to codex so it actually starts them.
- **Per-thread config pickup** (`b0bce14`) — root `mcpServers` moved from process-global app-server spawn `-c` overrides to each session's `thread/start.config.mcp_servers`. Because the codex app-server is process-global and spawned once, servers added to Host Settings *after* it started were never applied. Per-thread config merges with the user's global `~/.codex/config.toml`, so every new session reflects the current config without restarting the shared app-server — matching copilot's per-session model. A prewarmed-but-unused thread whose MCP set changed before its first turn is restarted to pick it up.

### OAuth-gated MCP servers (copilot parity)
- **Authenticate via the workbench** (`08d9f13`) — an auth-gated http server (e.g. an eng-hub server) reached codex but failed with "not logged in". The agent now reports it as `McpServerStatus.AuthRequired` through the shared `McpCustomizationController` (so the workbench renders the same "Authenticate" affordance it uses for copilot), receives the acquired bearer via `IAgent.handleAuthenticationToken`, injects it into the per-thread `http_headers.Authorization`, and reconnects the affected threads (lossless `thread/start` pre-first-turn, `thread/resume` with the current config otherwise). Verified against the real codex binary: it forwards `http_headers` on every MCP HTTP request.
- **Discover OAuth metadata** (`bc31a80`) — clicking "Authenticate" did nothing because the workbench's `resolveMcpServerAuthentication` needs the resource's `authorization_servers`, which codex's failure notification omits (unlike the copilot SDK, which discovers it internally). The agent now fetches the RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata (`<url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and carries `authorization_servers` + `scopes_supported` into the `AuthRequired` state, so the one-click sign-in completes.

### Customizations parity
- **Surface `.agents` skills + hooks** (`8312e63`) — codex natively reads `.agents/skills` (repo + user scope); these plus hooks now appear in the Customizations view via `skills/list` + `hooks/list`.
- **Ingest client-pushed plugin customizations** (`21ab6811`) — client "Open Plugins" are materialized + parsed via the shared `IAgentPluginManager` + `pluginParsers`, projected to the AHP `PluginCustomization` surface, with MCP servers attached per-session and skills fed via process-global `skills/extraRoots/set`.

### Diagnosability
- **MCP logging** (`5aad963`) — logs the MCP server names passed at `thread/start`, each `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated` transition (incl. auth/error), and the refreshed inventory with per-server state + tool counts.

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck-client` clean; **31 codex unit tests** pass (new pure helpers: `codexMcpServersFromConfig`, `normalizeCodexMcpResourceUrl`, `codexStartupErrorNeedsAuth`, `injectCodexMcpAuthTokens`); hygiene clean.
- Verified end-to-end in the Agents window: config-added-after-start servers are now picked up, and the OAuth "Authenticate" flow completes for an auth-gated http server (user-confirmed).
- Consumption paths (per-thread config, header forwarding, resume-with-config, RFC 9728 discovery) verified against the real codex binary.

## Notes
- Config changes apply to **new** sessions (and a prewarmed-unused one), not retroactively to a session already mid-conversation — matches copilot.
- Draft: opening for review/CI.

auto_merge.commit_message:
* codex: launch workbench-configured MCP servers via -c overrides

The codex agent read back MCP servers that the app-server already knew from
the user's global ~/.codex/config.toml, but never told codex which servers to
run. Configure the app-server with the workbench's root `mcpServers` config
(the same source the Copilot agent forwards to its SDK) so those servers are
actually launched and their tools become usable.

- Add buildCodexMcpServerOverrides() in codexMcpServers.ts: converts the root
  mcpServers config into codex `-c mcp_servers.<name>={...}` TOML overrides,
  with a minimal TOML encoder and per-entry validation (maps headers ->
  http_headers, drops the workbench-only type discriminator, stringifies env,
  skips malformed entries and names codex cannot address in a -c key path).
- Wire _buildMcpServerOverrides() into the app-server spawn args in codexAgent.
- Add unit tests for the encoder/validation.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: surface .agents skills + hooks in the Customizations view

Codex natively discovers skills from the VS Code `.agents/skills` convention
(repo + user scope) and hooks from `.codex`, but the agent only surfaced MCP
servers to the workbench Customizations view. Enumerate codex's effective
skills and hooks via the cwd-scoped `skills/list` / `hooks/list` app-server
methods and project them into DirectoryCustomization containers so what codex
loaded is visible alongside the MCP servers.

- Add codexCustomizations.ts: pure mappers codexSkillsToContainers (grouped by
  scope, de-duped by path) and codexHooksToContainers (de-duped by key).
- getSessionCustomizations() appends the skill/hook containers (best-effort when
  the connection is ready); _materialize() pushes SessionCustomizationUpdated so
  the view refreshes once the app-server connection comes up.
- Add codexCustomizations.test.ts unit tests.

Verified end-to-end against the real codex binary: a repo `.agents/skills`
skill is reported by skills/list and surfaces as a Skill customization under
the Repository container.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: ingest client-pushed plugin customizations

The codex active-client customizations setter was a no-op, so client-pushed
("Open Plugin") customizations the workbench synced were dropped. Wire them up
the way the Copilot and Claude agents already do, adapted to codex's
process-global app-server:

- Materialize + parse each client plugin via the shared IAgentPluginManager +
  pluginParsers (same components Claude/Copilot use), stored per session in a
  new CodexClientCustomizationStore with a per-customization enablement overlay.
- Surface the plugins (with their skill/MCP/agent/instruction/hook children) in
  getSessionCustomizations and honor setCustomizationEnabled toggles.
- Feed each plugin's MCP servers per-session via thread/start.config.mcp_servers
  (verified against the real codex binary: the server starts for that thread
  only), so a plugin's server runs only for sessions that enable it.
- Feed each plugin's skills via the process-global skills/extraRoots/set as the
  union of enabled skill roots across live sessions (codex has no per-thread
  skill-roots knob; this matches the global nature of client plugin choices).

Inject IAgentPluginManager / IFileService / INativeEnvironmentService (already
registered where CodexAgent is created). Hooks and custom agents are surfaced
but not yet fed to codex.

Verified end-to-end against the real codex binary: a plugin's skills/extraRoots
skill appears in skills/list and its thread/start.config MCP server appears in
mcpServerStatus/list. Agents window boots and registers codex with the new deps.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: apply root MCP servers per-thread so config changes are picked up

The codex agent baked the workbench root `mcpServers` config into the
app-server's `-c mcp_servers.<name>=<toml>` spawn overrides. Because the
app-server is process-global and spawned once, servers added to Host
Settings after the app-server started were never applied (and the TOML
override key parser could not address names with dots/whitespace).

Move root `mcpServers` from the process-global spawn overrides to each
session's `thread/start.config.mcp_servers`, merged with that session's
enabled client-plugin servers. codex applies `config.mcp_servers` as
per-thread overrides that merge with the user's global
`~/.codex/config.toml`, so every new session now reflects the current
root config without restarting the shared app-server -- matching the
copilot agent's per-session model. A prewarmed-but-unused thread whose
MCP set changed before its first turn is restarted to pick up the new
servers (same mechanism already used for client tools).

Replaces the TOML string encoder with a JSON producer
(`codexMcpServersFromConfig` / `toCodexMcpServerJson`) since per-thread
config takes structured JSON; server names with dots/whitespace are now
valid (they are JSON object keys, not `-c` override key segments).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: log MCP server wiring + startup status for diagnosability

The per-thread MCP refactor dropped the "configuring N MCP servers" log,
leaving no signal for whether a workbench-configured server actually
reached codex or what state it settled into. Add three concise info
logs: the MCP server names passed at `thread/start`, each
`mcpServer/startupStatus/updated` transition (with any error), and the
post-refresh inventory (per-server state + tool count). This makes an
auth/connection failure of an http MCP server (e.g. an OAuth-gated
endpoint) visible in the agent host log instead of silently surfacing as
"no MCP servers" in the model's reply.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: authenticate OAuth-gated MCP servers via the workbench (copilot parity)

An OAuth-gated http MCP server (e.g. the eng-hub server at mcp.eng.ms)
reached codex but failed to start with "not logged in", because codex
won't expose an unauthenticated server's tools. The Copilot agent makes
the same server work by reporting it as `AuthRequired`, letting the
workbench acquire an OAuth bearer token (VS Code dynamic client
registration), and injecting that token into the connection. Bring the
same mechanism to codex.

- Detect the auth failure: a `failed` `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated`
  whose error indicates sign-in is required now surfaces as
  `McpServerStatus.AuthRequired` (with the server URL as the OAuth
  `resource`) via the shared `McpCustomizationController`, so the
  workbench renders the same "Authenticate" affordance it uses for
  Copilot.
- Receive the token: implement `IAgent.handleAuthenticationToken` on the
  codex agent. When the workbench completes sign-in, the fanned-out
  `authenticate` command delivers the bearer; codex stores it keyed by
  the normalized server URL (process-global, so it applies to every
  session/thread on the shared app-server).
- Inject + reconnect: `_buildSessionMcpServers` adds
  `http_headers.Authorization: Bearer <token>` for any server with a
  stored token. Affected threads reconnect -- a pre-first-turn thread is
  restarted (lossless), one with history resumes with the current
  `config.mcp_servers` on its next turn (`thread/resume` carries the same
  `config` field). Verified against the real codex binary: it forwards
  `http_headers` on every MCP HTTP request, so a 401-gated server is
  rejected without the bearer and connects (exposing its tools) with it.

New pure, unit-tested helpers in codexMcpServers.ts:
`normalizeCodexMcpResourceUrl`, `codexStartupErrorNeedsAuth`,
`injectCodexMcpAuthTokens`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: discover MCP OAuth metadata so the workbench Authenticate action works

Clicking "Authenticate" on an auth-gated codex MCP server (e.g. via MCP:
List Servers) did nothing: the workbench's `resolveMcpServerAuthentication`
iterates `ProtectedResourceMetadata.authorization_servers` and returns
early when it is empty, and the metadata codex synthesized carried only
`{ resource, resource_name }`. codex's `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated`
failure omits the RFC 9728 challenge, so unlike the Copilot SDK (which
discovers the metadata internally) we had no authorization server to sign
in against.

Discover it: when surfacing an auth-gated server as `AuthRequired`, fetch
its Protected Resource Metadata from
`<url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (base `fetchResourceMetadata`,
15s timeout) and carry the resulting `authorization_servers` +
`scopes_supported` in the `AuthRequired` state. The workbench then runs the
exact same OAuth (dynamic client registration -> browser sign-in) it uses
for Copilot, and the acquired bearer flows back through
`handleAuthenticationToken`. Discovery failure still surfaces `AuthRequired`
with bare metadata (the server genuinely needs auth) and is logged.

This makes `_handleMcpStartupStatus` -> auth handling asynchronous: the
server stays in its prior (starting) state until discovery resolves, then
settles into `AuthRequired`. Verified the discovery step against the
compiled base helper (well-known PRM doc -> authorization_servers).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* codex: harden MCP config/auth handling and fix a Windows-only test

Addresses review feedback on the MCP integration plus a cross-platform
test bug:

- Fix Windows unit test: `codexSkillRootsFromPlugins` returns native
  fsPaths (backslashes on Windows), so the test now derives the expected
  roots via the same `URI.file(...).fsPath` transform instead of a
  hardcoded posix path. (This was the failing `Windows / Electron` check.)

- Route auth tokens by OAuth resource, not server URL: RFC 9728 discovery
  can return a `resource` that differs from the configured server endpoint
  (e.g. root `https://host/` for a `https://host/mcp` server). We now
  record a resource -> server-URL association when surfacing `AuthRequired`
  and resolve the pushed token through it (keeping a direct-URL fallback),
  so the bearer is injected for the right server even when they differ.

- Re-prompt on a rejected token: an expired/revoked/insufficient-scope
  token previously suppressed `AuthRequired` and became a terminal error
  with no way to re-auth. A repeated auth failure now clears the stored
  token and re-surfaces `AuthRequired`.

- Sanitize untrusted server config: `args`/`env`/`http_headers` values are
  coerced to the string shapes codex requires (and non-string `cwd`
  dropped), so a malformed Host Settings entry can't make codex reject the
  whole per-thread config.

- Strip a pre-existing case-insensitive `authorization` header before
  injecting the bearer, so a configured lowercase `authorization` can't
  leave a stale credential alongside the injected one.

`code --telemetry` omitted standalone telemetry schemas shipped by bundled extensions, including GitHub Copilot Chat.

- **Built-in collection**
  - Scan `builtinExtensionsPath` for `telemetry.json`.
  - Derive source identity from the extension manifest:

    ```text
    <publisher>.<name>-<version>
    ```
- **Precedence**
  - Merge user-installed schemas after built-ins so matching user extensions deterministically override bundled versions.

- **Coverage**
  - Cover manifest-based identity, built-in inclusion, user precedence, ignored schema-less built-ins, and existing schema sources.

title: voice: NACK + client revalidation for dropped narration
body:
fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8430

Stacked on #325928. Because the ordering branch lives only in the fork, this PR is opened against the same base as #325928, so it shows two commits: the ordering commit from #325928 and the NACK commit added here. Review only the top commit, `voice: NACK + client revalidation for dropped narration`; it lands once #325928 merges.

## Problem

Client-driven narration (`request_narration`) can be dropped by the backend and never recovered. When the backend cannot play a requested narration right now (the user is speaking, or a reply is in flight) it silently discards the request, so the confirmation prompt or reply summary is never read. The same silence happens when an in-flight narration is cut off by barge-in. The client had no way to learn about either case, so the only recovery was an unrelated later state change.

## Solution

Implement the client half of the NACK + revalidation protocol the backend now speaks:

- Handle `narration_ack` (`accepted` / `busy` / `invalid`). `accepted` is a no-op; `invalid` is dropped; `busy` defers the narration.
- On `busy` or `narration_interrupted`, remember the narration per session (latest-wins, one pending narration per session).
- On `narration_unblocked` (a content-free server nudge sent once the playback guard clears), revalidate the deferred narration against the current session state via the existing `_currentNarratable` oracle and re-request only if it is still warranted. The same narration id is reused when the text is unchanged so the backend can dedup a lost ack and avoid double-speak.
- Clear a deferred narration when the session starts a new turn (`thinking`) or on teardown.

The `narration_unblocked` nudge is server-driven and mode-agnostic, so it recovers narration in both push-to-talk and hands-free without any client timer.

## Tests

Manual, against a GA voice-code backend carrying the matching server change (`infinity-microsoft/yolo#55139`). Verified: busy -> unblock -> revalidate -> audio; barge-in -> interrupted -> revalidate; and a narration that is no longer warranted is dropped without speaking. The VS Code voice client has no unit-test harness for the controller, consistent with the prior PRs in this series.

## Risks

- If a `narration_unblocked` nudge is lost, the deferred narration is only recovered by the next session state change. This matches today's behavior for a lost narration and is strictly better than the current permanent silence.
- Revalidation depends on `_currentNarratable` reflecting current state; a stale confirmation detail would drop rather than mis-speak (fail-safe).

## Non-goals

- No change to the backend (shipped separately in `infinity-microsoft/yolo#55139`).
- No change to the auto-narrate opt-out (#325799) or the ordering gate (#325928).
- No new client timers or polling.

title: sessions: keep new-session config chips visible (disabled) while a draft re-resolves
body:
## Problem

In the Agents window new-session composer, switching the **workspace folder** or the **agent** (copilot / claude / codex) made the **Isolation (worktree) checkbox** and **Branch chip** disappear, show a spinner, then reappear once config resolved.

Switching creates a brand-new draft whose config schema is momentarily empty, so `AgentHostSessionConfigPicker` rendered no chips until the async `resolveSessionConfig` round-trip landed.

## Fix

Cache the well-known config-property schemas and re-inject them (disabled) while a new draft is still resolving, so the chips stay visible and re-enable with resolved values instead of blanking. The existing "disable during resolve" path handles the disabled state; the chips' values are left untouched during the load. Also added a resolving guard to the mobile unified-sheet path.

The caching mechanism is generic (`CACHED_CONFIG_KEYS`) — currently isolation + branch, but any well-known key added there gets the same behavior.

## Test

Added a DOM-rendering test asserting the chips stay visible + disabled during a resolve and re-enable with resolved values.

title: voice: send request_narration only after session context is sent
body:
Stacked on #325682 (base = `megrogge/voice-backend-narrate-api`), follow-up to the auto-narrate opt-out from #325799.

## Problem
`requestNarration` only checks that the socket is `OPEN`. A focus- or state-driven narration can therefore be sent in the window between the WebSocket opening and `start_session` / `resume_session` being sent. The backend drops a `request_narration` that arrives before the session exists, but the client still gets a narration id back and treats the audio as inbound: it tears down listening via `_prepareForPlayback`, records a solicited narration id, and arms a safety timer for audio that never arrives. The narration is not queued for replay, so it is lost until the next focus/state event.

## Solution
Track whether `start_session` / `resume_session` (which carries `session_context`) has been sent on the current connection (`_sessionContextSent`, reset per connection in `onopen`, set after each send) and gate `requestNarration` on it. The WebSocket preserves send order, so this guarantees the backend has processed the session before it sees a narration request. Pre-session, `requestNarration` now returns `undefined`, so `_narrate` queues the item in `_pendingNarrationRetries` and `onSessionInit` replays it once the session exists — reusing the existing retry path.

## Tests
None. This file has no existing unit tests and the change is a small ordering guard on the WS send path; adding a WebSocket-mocking harness for it is out of scope for this follow-up. Verified by tracing the client/backend ordering and the `_narrate` / `onSessionInit` replay interaction.

## Risks
Low. Behavior only changes in the pre-session-init window: narration is deferred to `session_init` replay instead of being sent-then-dropped. Steady-state narration is unaffected (`_sessionContextSent` is true once the session is established).

## Non-goals
No backend changes; no change to the narration payload or the `auto_narrate` opt-out.

title: Phase 10.6: MCP elicitation (real `onElicitation` translation)
body:
## What

Replaces the Phase-7 `onElicitation` cancel-stub for the Claude agent with a real translation. When an MCP server (the host's own in-process server, or a third-party server) calls `elicit/create`, the request now **surfaces to the user** as structured input instead of being silently auto-cancelled, and the user's answer is delivered back to the server as an `ElicitResult`.

Before:
```ts
onElicitation: async req => {
	logElicitation(req.message ?? '');
	return { action: 'cancel' };   // silently declined
},
```

## How

Elicitation routes through the **same structured user-input channel `AskUserQuestion` already uses** (`requestUserInput` → `ActionType.ChatInputRequested` → `respondToUserInputRequest`), **not** the `pending_confirmation` permission gate (design locked in `CONTEXT.md`).

- **`claudeElicitation.ts`** (new) — pure projections: JSON-Schema → `ChatInputQuestion[]` and workbench answers → `ElicitResult.content`. Each field is runtime-validated with the base-layer `vs/base/common/validation.ts` (drops malformed fields instead of throwing); the field type is *derived* from that validator and pinned to the MCP SDK's authoritative `PrimitiveSchemaDefinition` by a compile-time guard, so it can't drift from the spec.
- **`claudeElicitationBridge.ts`** (new) — `handleElicitation` looks up the session, parks on `requestUserInput`, observes the SDK per-request abort signal, and maps the response back to an `ElicitResult`. `decline` is reserved for an explicit user Decline; no-session / teardown / abort all map to `cancel`.
- Wire `onElicitation` through `IBuildOptionsInput` → `Options.onElicitation`, `IMaterializeContext`, and `ClaudeAgent._makeOnElicitation` — exactly mirroring `canUseTool`. The `logElicitation` stub param is removed.
- **`form`** mode (schema → questions) and **`url`** mode (question-less request carrying the URL) are both supported.

## Scope notes

- `SDKElicitationCompleteMessage` (out-of-band URL completion) is intentionally **out of scope** — the promise-await model already resolves URL prompts via the existing `ChatInputCompleted` path.
- Subagent-scoped routing (`parentToolCallId`) is out of scope; elicitation carries no `agentID`.
- No change to the `IAgent` public surface or the protocol `ChatInputRequest` shape.

Full step-by-step design + decisions: [`phase10.6-plan.md`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/tyleonha/claude-phase-10.6-mcp-elicitation/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/phase10.6-plan.md).

## Testing

- **Unit** (`claudeElicitation.test.ts`, 11): every field kind + branch (text/number/integer/boolean/oneOf/enum±enumNames/array items.enum+anyOf/unknown+missing type), url mode, malformed-schema and every empty/broken-form → message-only degradation, per-field validation drop, accept/decline/cancel mapping, accept edge cases, bridge no-session → cancel.
- **Agent** (`claudeAgent.test.ts` Phase 10.6, 5): form accept round-trip, decline, abort-mid-park, url-mode round-trip, pre-aborted signal.
- **Integration** (`claudeAgent.integrationTest.ts` §5.3): real accept round-trip through the proxy-backed materialize → Options boundary.
- **Manual E2E**: verified live in the Agents window driving real Claude Opus against `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` — `trigger-elicitation-request` renders a 13-field form.

Local gate green: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, eslint, full agentHost unit suite (2725), claude integration (5), claude protocol e2e (8).

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324243, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325150,

title: Collapse Agent Host per-session GitHub telemetry token map to the singleton token
body:
Follow-up to #325722 (restricted model telemetry routing in the Agent Host).

## What
Removes the per-session `_githubTokensBySdkSession` map and resolves the restricted telemetry context from `this._githubToken` directly in `_routeGitHubTelemetry`. Drops the associated `register`/`rollback` plumbing and the `clear`/`delete` calls across every launch and teardown path.

## Why
Addresses review feedback on #325722: *"There's only 1 auth token for all sessions. It's `this._githubToken`."*

That's accurate for VS Code today — VS Code only ever sources a single `_githubToken` and snapshots that same value into every session's launch plan, so the map held the same token under every session id and added lifecycle plumbing without changing behavior.

The map was there to match the runtime's session-scoped auth (the runtime supports distinct per-session tokens and live `setCredentials`), but VS Code doesn't exercise that path — sessions get the token once at launch and never swap it — so a divergent per-session token can't occur here. If per-session tokens are ever wired up from VS Code, this can be reintroduced against that concrete need.

The no-token / BYOK case stays fail-safe on both ends: no GitHub token → the router emits nothing restricted, and the runtime independently gates on `copilotUser`.

## Behavior
No functional change for current single-account usage. A token refresh / account change is now reflected by resolving each event's context from the current token (verified by the rewritten routing test).

## Validation
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "CopilotAgent"` — 304 passing

title: editor: consolidate diff-editor command handlers into IDiffEditorCommandsService
body:
## What

Tech-debt follow-up to #325382. Moves the remaining inline diff-editor command handlers out of `diffEditorCommands.ts` and into `IDiffEditorCommandsService`, matching the delegation pattern already established for `toggleRenderSideBySide`.

Handlers moved into the service (command handlers now delegate via `accessor.get(IDiffEditorCommandsService).<method>(...)`):
- `DIFF_OPEN_SIDE` -> `openActiveDiffSide()`
- `GOTO_NEXT_CHANGE` / `GOTO_PREVIOUS_CHANGE` -> `navigateInDiffEditor(args, next)`
- `DIFF_FOCUS_PRIMARY_SIDE` / `DIFF_FOCUS_SECONDARY_SIDE` / `DIFF_FOCUS_OTHER_SIDE` -> `focusInDiffEditor(args, mode)` (with the `FocusTextDiffEditorMode` enum now exported from the service)
- `TOGGLE_DIFF_IGNORE_TRIM_WHITESPACE` -> `toggleDiffIgnoreTrimWhitespace(args)`
- `DIFF_SWAP_SIDES` -> `swapDiffSides(args)`

## Why

`diffEditorCommands.ts` previously mixed command registration with inline handler logic that resolved services through `ServicesAccessor`. Consolidating the behavior into the service keeps command registration thin, centralizes the diff-editor logic in one place, and lets the Agents window override behavior where needed (today only `toggleRenderSideBySide`, for the multi-diff Changes editor).

## Notes for reviewers

- Services are injected in the service constructor rather than resolved via `ServicesAccessor` inside each method.
- Methods that perform config writes (`toggleDiffIgnoreTrimWhitespace`, `swapDiffSides`, `openActiveDiffSide`) are `async`/return `Promise<void>` and the command handlers return the promise, so failures propagate (consistent with the `toggleRenderSideBySide` change in #325382).
- The `getActiveTextDiffEditor` / `getActiveDiffModifiedResource` resolver helpers are now **private methods** on the service (they no longer have any external callers).
- `SessionsDiffEditorCommandsService` (Agents window) is unchanged: it still overrides only `toggleRenderSideBySide` and inherits the newly-consolidated methods from the base class. The other operations act on a single diff editor and need no Agents-window override.
- Adds `diffEditorCommandsService.test.ts` covering `navigateInDiffEditor`, `focusInDiffEditor` (incl. toggle), and `toggleDiffIgnoreTrimWhitespace`. `swapDiffSides` / `openActiveDiffSide` orchestrate `editorService.replaceEditors`/`findEditors`/`openEditor` and aren't meaningfully unit-testable with lightweight fakes.

title: sessions: avoid force-opening managed tabs when opening a file in single-pane layout
body:
## What & why

In the Agents window **single-pane layout**, opening a file (from chat or quick-pick) would force-open the managed **Changes** + **Files** docked tabs — so after closing them, opening a file re-added them and the side pane could no longer be closed by closing that file.

This reworks the single-pane managed docked tabs so the default tabs are opened **only into an empty editor group** on a genuine *view-open* trigger, removing the fragile dismissal-tracking and aux-bar-visibility inference.

## Key changes

- **New layout-service events** (in `workbench.ts` / base controller): `onDidRevealSidePane` (side pane transitions fully-hidden → visible) and `onDidEndSessionLayoutRestore` (restore epoch settles). The managed-tabs strategy is driven off named triggers **A–D**.
- **Open defaults only into an empty group** — closing a managed tab now sticks; opening/closing a file no longer re-forces the tabs, so closing the last tab still closes the side pane.
- **Submit** (uncreated → created) ensures the **Changes** tab, opened *active* (so the detail panel maps to it).
- **Details-only reveal** (aux detail shown without the editor area) ensures all docked inputs even in a non-empty group.
- **Reconcile intents scoped per session** — a reconcile superseded by a session switch cannot leak its "activate Changes"/"ensure inputs" intent onto the switched-to session.
- **Responsive sessions-list** auto-collapse gated to small windows (`≤ 1800px`); restored when the window grows.
- **Editor-collapse on hide** only happens for a details-only hide (aux still visible), not when the whole side pane closes (so editors are preserved).

## Notes for reviewers

- `SinglePaneManagedTabsStrategy` was rewritten around explicit triggers + a linear `_reconcile` for readability; behavior is documented in `SINGLE_PANE_SCENARIOS.md` and the sessions `SKILL.md` pitfall.
- All changes are scoped to `src/vs/sessions`.

## Validation

- `gulp compile-client`: 0 errors
- Full `vs/sessions` browser suite: **1458 passing, 18 pending, 0 failing** (incl. a new async session-switch leak regression test that fails on the old behavior)
- `typecheck-client` and `valid-layers-check`: clean
- ESLint on changed files: clean

title: Automations: remove lingering :has() selectors from dialog and list
body:
## Context

Follow-up to #324986 (which fixed #324985), the fix that removed the catastrophic `body:has(.automation-dialog)` rules causing persistent workbench-wide style-recalc jank. That PR removed the worst offenders, but the Automations UI still shipped **four** `:has()` selectors in [`aiCustomizationManagement.css`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/media/aiCustomizationManagement.css). This is the audit follow-up that removes the rest.

This stylesheet is imported by eagerly-loaded chat-contrib modules, so its rules live in the global document stylesheet whenever the chat contrib is loaded — present in Stable even when the Automations feature is off (`chat.automations.enabled` defaults to `false`).

## What changed

All four remaining `:has()` selectors are gone (a `:has(` grep now matches only explanatory comments):

| Rule (before) | After |
|---|---|
| `.action-item:has(.action-label.codicon-{settings,add,server})` — hides 3 embedded chat-input chips | Dropped **at the source** via a new `hiddenInputToolbarActionIds` `ChatInputPart` option (rendered as `HiddenActionViewItem`). No CSS needed. |
| `.automations-row:has(:focus-visible)` | `.automations-row:focus-within` |
| `.automations-row-wrapper:has(> .automations-row-history)` (×2) | JS-toggled `.automations-row-wrapper-expanded` class |

### Why the chip rule mattered most
`.action-item` is a workbench-wide element and `codicon-settings/add/server` are common toolbar icons, so `.action-item:has(.action-label.codicon-*)` registered `:has()` invalidation bookkeeping keyed on common classes across the whole workbench — the same bug family as the fixed `body:has()`, just lower severity (anchor is `.action-item`, not `body`). Hiding those chips at the view-item level (the codebase's established `HiddenActionViewItem` mechanism, already used for the phone Mode picker) removes them from layout and keyboard tab order with no `:has()`.

### Incidental fix
The `.automations-row-history` element is **always** present in the DOM, so `:has(> .automations-row-history)` matched *every* row regardless of expanded state — meaning collapsed rows silently lost their hover highlight and always had flattened bottom corners. The new `.automations-row-wrapper-expanded` class (toggled in `automationsListWidget.ts` `renderElement`) reflects the actual expanded state, restoring hover highlight on collapsed rows and only flattening the card corners when the run-history panel is expanded — which matches the original CSS comment's intent.

## Notes for reviewers
- No functional change to the chips shown in other chat surfaces — the hide is scoped to the automation dialog's `ChatInputPart` instance.
- `.action-item` elements are still `display:none` (via `HiddenActionViewItem`), identical DOM ordering to before, so the existing inter-chip divider-suppression rule remains valid.
- Two intentional visual behavior changes to spot-check: (1) collapsed automation rows now show a hover highlight; (2) the row focus ring now also appears on mouse-click focus of a row action button (`:focus-within` vs keyboard-only `:focus-visible`), consistent with the sibling tools/prompts lists' documented pattern.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passes
- ESLint on changed TS — passes
- stylelint on the CSS — passes (only pre-existing design-token suggestions, none introduced)
- Pre-commit hygiene — passes

Draft while I run through the local visual test pass (enable `chat.automations.enabled`, open **Open Customizations → Automations**, exercise list hover/focus/expand and the create/edit dialog toolbar).

title: sessions: fix docked detail panel gap at bottom in single-pane layout
body:
## What

In the Agents window single-pane layout, the docked detail panel (the auxiliary bar reparented into the editor area) was laid out with a gap at the bottom — its content didn't fill the full height of the docked rectangle.

## Why

`SinglePaneAuxiliaryBarPart` intentionally renders **no title strip** (the single tab bar lives on the editor part), but it inherited `hasTitle: true` from the base `AuxiliaryBarPart`. `PartLayout.layout` still subtracts the title height (~35px) from the content area whenever `hasTitle` is true — even though no title area actually exists. So the composite content was sized ~35px shorter than its container, leaving the empty gap.

## Fix

Override `create()` in `SinglePaneAuxiliaryBarPart` to clear `hasTitle` before the part layout is built, so the content fills the full docked rectangle. This also lets the base `createTitleArea` return `undefined` on its own, so the now-redundant `createTitleArea` override was removed.

## Notes for reviewers

- Change is confined to `src/vs/sessions/`.
- Typechecks clean and passes the layers checker.

title: Emit v2 cloud agent sessionActivated telemetry from live task stream
body:
## Problem

The v2 (Task API) cloud agent backend never emitted the `copilotcloud.chat.sessionActivated` funnel signal, so the v1-vs-v2 activation funnel (time-to-first-turn / activation rate) could not be compared in telemetry.

Root cause: the only call site for `sessionActivated` on v2 lived inside `TaskApiBackend.waitForTaskUpdate`, which had **no callers**. v1 emits the equivalent signal from `waitForJobWithPullRequest` during `createSession` — hence the asymmetry.

## Approach

A provider-owned **activation monitor** is started the moment a v2 task is created (`startTaskActivationMonitor`, wired into the delegation helper). It polls the task and emits `sessionActivated` once the task produces its first turn — the v2 analogue of v1's PR becoming available — then stops.

Key properties:

- **Reported regardless of the UI.** The monitor runs independently of whether the user opens the session, so freshly-created zero-session tasks and fast-finishing tasks are captured (not only tasks that happen to be live-streamed).
- **`activations ≤ creations` preserved.** Monitors are armed **only for locally-created tasks**, so activation can't be reported without a matching local `sessionCreate`. Monitors are cancelled on provider dispose; an ext-host reload drops them (under-count) rather than risking a double-count. State is intentionally not persisted — for a funnel, over-counting is worse than a missed activation.
- **Requires real output.** Activation fires only when an `assistant.*` event is observed (genuine turn output) and is suppressed for tasks that reach a terminal state with no output (e.g. "Failed to launch agent"), so no-output failures don't inflate the funnel.
- **`durationMs`** is measured from the task's `created_at` (falling back to monitor start ≈ creation time).

The `TaskTurnStreamer` remains a pure renderer with no telemetry dependency.

## Cleanup

- Removed the dead `waitForTaskUpdate` (method, `TaskCloudAgentBackend` interface declaration, unused poll constants).
- Removed the now-dead `pollUpdate` operation from the `CloudBackendOperation` union and from `agent_monitoring.md` (its only emitter was `waitForTaskUpdate`).

## Validation

- `tsgo` type-check: clean for all changed files.
- ESLint: clean.
- `copilotCloudSessionsProvider.spec.ts`: 32/32 passing.

title: Claude agent: allow 'max' reasoning effort on the runtime path
body:
## What

`clampEffortForRuntime` now passes `max` reasoning effort straight through instead of degrading it to `xhigh` on the runtime (`applyFlagSettings`) path.

## Why

The SDK's `Settings.effortLevel` type — reused by `Query.applyFlagSettings({ effortLevel })` — is typed `low | medium | high | xhigh`, omitting `max`. That type is wrong: the Anthropic API / Copilot CAPI accept `max` end-to-end (the exported `EffortLevel` union and the wire `output_config.effort` field both include it). Confirmed with Anthropic and verified live — a `max` turn on Claude Opus 4.8 puts `output_config.effort:"max"` on the CAPI `/v1/messages` call and returns success. Previously a mid-session `max` pick was silently clamped to `xhigh`.

## How

- `clampEffortForRuntime` keeps its narrow `ClaudeRuntimeEffortLevel` return type but returns `max` at runtime via a single, documented cast — every downstream consumer stays typed against the SDK's declared surface while the one lie is contained in one place.
- Removed the now-incorrect `max`->`xhigh` warning in `setModel`.
- Tests updated to assert `max` passes through.

## Follow-up

Upstream SDK typing fix tracked at anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript#377 — drop the cast once `Settings.effortLevel` includes `max`.

title: Fix Mermaid preview flash/disappear on rerender
body:
## Summary
- Persist canonical Mermaid diagram source in `data-vscode-mermaid-source` and fall back to `vscodeContext.mermaidSource` when container text is polluted by rendered SVG/CSS
- Detect rendered output via DOM children (`svg` / `.mermaid-error`) so rerenders no longer parse SVG style text as diagram source
- Surface Mermaid parse/render failures even when the rejection is a plain object (not an `Error`), so broken diagrams show an error instead of an empty box

Fixes #323522
Fixes #328449

## Root cause
On theme/content refresh, `renderMermaidBlocksInElement` re-read `.mermaid` `textContent`, which after first render can contain CSS from embedded SVG `<style>` tags. Mermaid then fails with errors like "No diagram type detected matching given configuration for text: #dmermaid-…". Those failures are often plain objects, so the old `instanceof Error` gate also left the container blank with no visible error.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a `.md` file with a fenced `mermaid` block in Markdown Preview
- [ ] Confirm diagram renders on first open
- [ ] Toggle color theme (or edit/save to refresh preview) — diagram should remain visible
- [ ] Repeat with flowchart and class diagram types
- [ ] Break the Mermaid syntax — preview should show a real error message, not an empty box
- [ ] Confirm no conflicting third-party Mermaid extensions are required for the repro (built-in path only)

title: Preserve inbound Anthropic PDF documents
body:
Fixes #325672

## Summary

- Preserve base64 PDF `document` blocks when parsing inbound Anthropic-compatible requests.
- Preserve PDF documents nested inside `tool_result` content.
- Redact base64 document payloads from request logging while retaining their media type.

## Problem

The `/v1/messages` endpoint parses Anthropic request bodies with `anthropicMessagesToRawMessages`. That converter handled text, images, thinking blocks, tool calls, and tool results, but it did not handle `document` blocks.

As a result, a top-level PDF was omitted before the request reached the selected model. When a PDF was the only user content, the resulting empty user message could also be omitted entirely. Documents nested inside `tool_result` content were similarly discarded because only text and image blocks were converted there.

## Fix

Base64 Anthropic document sources are now converted to the existing Raw document content part, preserving both the base64 data and `application/pdf` media type. The same conversion is used for top-level message content and tool-result content.

The downstream Messages and Responses request builders already support Raw PDF document parts, so no endpoint-specific conversion changes are required. The logging conversion now replaces document data with a placeholder, matching the existing image and tool-result sanitization behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-extensions`
- `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` in `extensions/copilot`
- `npm run test:unit -- src/extension/byok/common/test/anthropicMessageConverter.spec.ts`
- `npm run test:unit -- src/platform/endpoint/test/node/messagesApi.spec.ts src/platform/endpoint/node/test/responsesApi.spec.ts`
- `npx eslint src/extension/byok/common/anthropicMessageConverter.ts src/extension/byok/common/test/anthropicMessageConverter.spec.ts`

title: Simplify redundant nested ternary in notebook cell sort comparator
Draw attention to blocking input prompts
body:
Fixes #325764

### Problem

VS Code occasionally shows blocking input prompts (`window.showInputBox` / Quick Input) that must be answered before an operation can continue: git/ssh authentication, passphrase requests, API keys, extension configuration prompts, and so on.

These prompts render at the very top of the window, while the user's attention is usually on the terminal, editor, Debug Console, or an extension view. When the prompt is missed, the operation just waits for input, and it looks as though the terminal, an extension, or VS Code itself has frozen.

### Change

Briefly pulse the Quick Input widget when a blocking input prompt appears, so it is immediately obvious that input is required.

- The pulse is scoped to `QuickInputType.InputBox` (what `window.showInputBox` uses), so the **command palette** and **quick open** which the user opens intentionally are unaffected.
- Implemented as a short CSS ring animation on `.quick-input-widget` using `--vscode-focusBorder`, retriggered per prompt by toggling a `quick-input-needs-attention` class (with a forced reflow so it replays when the widget element is reused).
- Respects accessibility preferences: the animation is disabled under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.

### Details

- `quickInputController.show()` adds the `quick-input-needs-attention` class when the controller type is `InputBox`, and clears it on every show so quick picks never inherit it.
- Screen reader users are unaffected: focus already moves into the input box, so the prompt is announced as before.

### Notes

The animation approach is one of the ideas suggested in the issue. If maintainers prefer, it would be straightforward to gate this behind a setting (e.g. `workbench.quickInput.pulseOnInputPrompt`) or to also surface an accessibility signal. Happy to adjust based on direction.

### Verification

- `tsc`/language-server diagnostics clean on the changed files.
- Manual: git authentication / `showInputBox` prompts pulse once on appearance; command palette and quick open do not; no pulse with reduced motion enabled.

title: fix(network): align transient retry behavior and remove unnecessary Fetch Content-Length header
body:
Fixes #325820

## Summary

This PR contains two small networking-related fixes.

### 1. Align transient retry behavior in `AgentHostRequestService`

`AgentHostRequestService` retries several transient network failures but does not currently retry `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, or `ETIMEDOUT`.

Other networking components in the VS Code codebase already treat these errors as retryable. This change aligns the retry behavior for idempotent requests and adds regression tests to prevent future regressions.

### 2. Remove unnecessary `Content-Length` header from the Fetch path

The Fetch implementation in `OtlpHttpForwarder` explicitly sets the `Content-Length` request header.

Fetch implementations compute this header automatically, making it unnecessary to set manually. This change removes it only from the Fetch code path while leaving the `http.request()` implementation unchanged.

## Testing

- Added regression tests covering retries for:
  - `ECONNRESET`
  - `EPIPE`
  - `ETIMEDOUT`
- Verified retry behavior for idempotent requests.
